close_reason: Landed in commit 6cf54bc. Option (a) ratified: dropped JsContactId transparent newtype; Title.organization_id is now Option<String>; all RFC 9553 §1.4.1 Id references in the crate are bare String throughout (consistent with the consumer jmap-contacts-types Sloppy-Value pattern). Tests + clippy + rustdoc green on workspace. Closes sgrr.13, sgrr.23, sgrr.25 as moot (see those beads for individual close).
description: crate-jmap-jscontact-types/src/lib.rs:63 defines JsContactId as a transparent newtype around String. It is referenced in exactly ONE wire field: Title.organization_id at lib.rs:338. SpeakToAs.pronouns is typed Option<HashMap<String, Pronouns>> at lib.rs:280, but its doc comment at lib.rs:278 says 'Map of pronoun Id(JsContactId) → Pronouns object' — i.e. semantically it IS an Id-keyed map per RFC 9553 §2.2.4, but the Rust type uses bare String. This is either (a) a missed application of the newtype, or (b) a deliberate choice that the newtype only applies to scalar Id references, not to map keys. Either way it is inconsistent and not documented. Once published, changing SpeakToAs.pronouns to HashMap<JsContactId, Pronouns> is a breaking change. Decide now: either drop JsContactId entirely (it earns its keep nowhere meaningful at one usage site), or apply it consistently to SpeakToAs.pronouns keys (and document the policy for future Id-typed map keys).
title: JsContactId newtype used inconsistently — only Title.organization_id, not SpeakToAs.pronouns keys
